page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised under Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with two threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is 384.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, supported by a large 480 MB L3 cache. Local storage includes 5669 GB of direct NVMe SSD capacity, while GPU accelerators are absent.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing and enterprise I/O throughput. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 106546.32 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 596.61 GB/sec, placing it within the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Hardware acceleration capabilities such as AVX-512, AMX int8, and AMX tile instructions contribute to a PassMark extended instructions result of 123083.77 and rapid LLM prompt processing throughput of 312.2 tokens/sec on 7B models. Database operations and in-memory key-value processing reach top-tier status, highlighted by 156.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 151.5 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The 5669 GB NVMe SSD volume offers high-speed transient data access without remote storage network latency, making it cost-efficient for heavy read and write scratch environments. A hardware tradeoff appears in single-core compute tasks, where stress-ng scores average 2281.99, indicating performance scaling relies primarily on parallelization. The instance is suited for high-concurrency relational and in-memory databases, batch data transformation pipelines, large web application fleets, and CPU-based matrix operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 384.0 GB of system memory, a 480 MB L3 cache, and 5669 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage without attached GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core execution, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 106546.32, top-tier static web throughput of 151.5 GB/sec, and 156.15 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions enhances integer and matrix computations, including LLM prompt processing. The combined 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation and high-density local NVMe array make this instance appropriate for multi-threaded databases, distributed caching, ETL pipelines, and high-traffic web applications.
